title: orc-registry-event v1
description: ONE WRITE-ONCE RECORD OF THE ORC REGISTRY: something people decided about the list of Orcs the founder sees on Dash - that an Orc is on it, its name, its one-line domain, the order of the whole list, or that it left. The registry is a folder, <HordeHome>\orcs\registry\, holding one file per record named by its sequence number in ten digits, written by decisions/Store.ps1 exactly as the decisions store is (a record is written whole, given its name once by a move only one writer can win, and never rewritten or deleted); only orcs/Registry.ps1 writes it. The records in sequence order are the single source of truth: the current list is their fold, worked out each time, and the registry's VERSION is its last sequence number. What is DERIVED - open questions, sessions open, working, idle or blocked - is never stored. ON DISK: UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, one JSON object, ASCII only. VERSIONING: a record that does not match this schema is reported as unreadable by its sequence number and changes nothing. A record that matches the envelope and whose kind this version does not know was written by a later version: it is set aside and reported once for its kind. A change to an existing kind's data, or to this envelope, is a v2.

sequence.description: The record's place in the one total order, from 1. It must equal the number in the record's file name. The registry's version is the sequence of its last record: a write drawn from version N is written as N + 1, and a writer that finds N + 1 taken was drawn from a list that has moved.

kind.description: What happened: orc-registered, orc-named, orc-domain-set, orcs-ordered, orc-retired or orc-tier-set (the kind table of orcs/Registry.ps1); each kind's data is a definition below of the same name.

at.description: When the record was written, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, by the writer's clock. Order is the sequence, never this time.

actor.description: Which way the change came: cli (horde orcs at a command line) or fleet (the registry following the lanes folder: a new lane registered, a lane the fleet retired taken off). Later ways - the founder's signed command from the phone - are new labels, not a new version.

by.description: Who made the change, as far as it was proven: the session's own label in the fleet's registry when the command ran inside a session that could be proven (notices/Sender.ps1), else console. Recorded so every change is kept with who and when; it decides nothing.

data.description: What the kind carries, checked against the definition named for the kind.

letter.description: The Orc's letter as its status file said it when it was registered; empty when the file named none.

domain.description: The Orc's domain on one line: at most 80 printable ASCII characters, stored exactly as given. Empty clears it.

order.description: The main list, first to last: his priority order.

backBurner.description: The back-burner list below the divider, first to last. With order, it names every registered Orc not retired exactly once: a reorder is one record and never half applied.

reason.description: hand: taken off by horde orcs retire, and it stays off. fleet: its lane was retired in the lanes folder (status.retired.txt and no status.txt, fleet/StatusPanel.ps1); a lane that comes back is registered again, at the end.

tier.description: The Orc's tier, 1 or 2. Until one is set the dash carries tier null.

id.description: The lane's stable id: its folder's name in the lanes folder.

name.description: The name shown, 1 to 40 printable ASCII characters; by default Orc and its letter.
